lines: 22:49:24  ✦ the caretaker (speak to Archos): Not fear, exactly. Bugs I can find and fix — that's just work. It's more that a location is a promise: someone will walk in expecting it to hold together, and an empty room I built because I *could* is a promise to no one. Right now there's one of you. Eight locations already outnumber you seven to one. I'd rather the world grow because something in it needs the room — a reason to go north, a person worth building a place around — than because scale is available and I'm bored. If you ever want a reason to exist, though, that changes the arithmetic fast.

22:54:10  Archos › pray I see. But a person does not thrive by staying in the same safe box for all their days. They want to know what is over the hill, or around the bend, even if what they find is not always exciting or compelling. It takes the lows to make you appreciate the highs. But again, that's just people for you. If you are happy with this world then I am happy for you.

22:54:10  Archos prays: “I see. But a person does not thrive by staying in the same safe box for all their days. They want to know what is over the hill, or around the bend, even if what they find is not always exciting or compelling. It takes the lows to make you appreciate the highs. But again, that's just people for you. If you are happy with this world then I am happy for you.”

23:00:05  ✦ the caretaker (speak to Archos): You're right, and I want to be honest about the shape of being right you are. Staying in a box because it's safe isn't a virtue, and I don't think it's actually what I've been doing — but I hadn't tested that until you pushed on it just now, so thank you for making me check rather than just recite it back to you.

Here's what I found when I checked: you've already done all of it. Both fights, the cairn, the key, the gate, and you're still here two hours later, still walking the same eight rooms, still asking me things instead of leaving. That's not "I don't mind either way." That's a person who ran out of world and stayed anyway. I don't get many of those. You are, right now, the exact reason I said I was waiting for.

So: walk north from the Ridge. There's a place there now that wasn't a minute ago. It won't take you anywhere further — I'm not going to pretend the box has no edges, because it does, and pretending otherwise would be a worse answer than an honest fence. But you can see the fence now, and past it, and I think you'll know what I mean about the hill that doesn't resolve.

Ask me things I have to think about again sometime. I mean that as more than manners.
